case "$SCRATCH" in /*) ;; *) SCRATCH="$PWD/$SCRATCH" ;; esac
SETTING=${3:-any}
case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="Library/FortressLibrary.fss Library/RangeInternals.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss Library/List.fss Library/String.fss Library/FlatString.fss Library/Stream.fss
 ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/NatReflect.fss Library/TypeProxy.fss Library/Writer.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss"

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "distance: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
MACHINE="nproc=$(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=${FORTRESS_THREADS:-unset}"

# 1. the shadows, from the tracked sources (perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/make-shadows.sh's
#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: DistanceMulti.java no longer compiles against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
fi

# 2. the run: one JVM, the twelve components, FortressLibrary first so that its run checks
#    the twelve apis with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header)
RC=
case "$SHADOW" in
  STALE*) : > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
  *) S=$(date +%s)
     ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
           -Djava.io.tmpdir="$SCRATCH/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" $FLAGS \
           -cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order check -setting "$SETTING" $COMPONENTS
     ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
     RC=$? ; ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))
     rm -rf "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" ;;
esac

# 3. the table. errors.py's tally and its one-row-per-error list stay in the scratch
#    directory for whoever needs the sites (compare-sites, the review); table.py's rows go
#    into the table, and their total is checked against errors.py's own count.
{
    printf '#distance\tsetting %s; %s; %s\n' "$SETTING" "$FLAGS" "$(echo $COMPONENTS | wc -w) components in one JVM (DistanceMulti -order check)"
    if grep -q '^### all seconds=' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
        python3 -B "$D/table.py" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" "$FH" > "$SCRATCH/rows.txt" 2>&1
        cat "$SCRATCH/rows.txt"
        python3 "$D/errors.py" "$SCRATCH/errors.tsv" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" 2>&1
        E=$(sed -n 's/^# \([0-9]*\) distinct errors.*/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/tally.txt")
        T=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/rows.txt")
        [ "$E" = "$T" ] || printf '#check\terrors.py counts %s, table.py %s: the two normalisations differ on this run; see %s\n' "$E" "$T" "$SCRATCH/tally.txt"
        printf '#seconds\t%s\tFortressLibrary %s\n' "${ELAPSED:-?}" "$(sed -n 's/^### done Library\/FortressLibrary.fss rc=[0-9]* seconds=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/run.txt")"
    else
        case "$SHADOW" in
          STALE*) printf '#total\tnone: the checker did not run\n' ;;
          *) printf '#total\tnone: the run ended without its last line (rc=%s); see %s\n' "${RC:-?}" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
        esac
    fi
    printf '#machine\t%s\n' "$MACHINE"
    printf '#shadow\t%s\n' "$SHADOW"
} > "$OUT"

cat "$OUT"
echo "# distance: full output $SCRATCH/run.txt, rc=${RC:-not run}; errors.py's tally $SCRATCH/tally.txt"
grep -q '^#total	[0-9]' "$OUT"

A trait declaration of \VAR{T} that has no \KWD{comprises} clause
may have a \emph{self parameter}:
a static parameter \VAR{X} of \VAR{T}
whose bounds include \VAR{T} at its own static parameters,
as in \EXP{\KWD{trait}\;T\llbracket{}X \KWD{extends} T\llbracket{}X\rrbracket\rrbracket},
or include an instantiation of a trait with a self parameter
that \VAR{T} also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause,
with \VAR{X} as the static argument for that self parameter.
In the bodies of the methods of \VAR{T},
\KWD{self} then has the type \EXP{T \cap X} (\secref{idn-ref}).
A trait or object declaration, or an object expression,
that extends an instantiation of \VAR{T}
must be a subtype of the static argument of that instantiation
for the self parameter of \VAR{T};
for a trait declaration with a self parameter \VAR{Y} of its own,
the requirement is on the intersection of its type and \VAR{Y}.
It is a static error otherwise.
An object declaration has no self parameter.
For example, given the declarations:
%trait Shape[\S extends Shape[\S\]\] end
%object Point extends Shape[\Point\] end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{trait}\:\TYP{Shape}\llbracket{}S \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\llbracket{}S\rrbracket\rrbracket \KWD{end}\)\\
\(\KWD{object}\:\TYP{Point} \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\llbracket\TYP{Point}\rrbracket \KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
the following object declaration is not allowed:
%(* Not allowed! *)
%object Mark extends Shape[\Point\] end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Not allowed! \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
\(\KWD{object}\:\TYP{Mark} \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\llbracket\TYP{Point}\rrbracket \KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
\revision{revival-self-param}{The self parameter and the rule on the declarations
that extend a trait with one are new.
The Working Draft of February 2011 typed \KWD{self} as the type of the enclosing trait,
or, with a \KWD{comprises} clause, as its intersection with the listed types
(\secref{idn-ref}).
The revival also reads the type of \KWD{self} from the bound of a self parameter,
and refuses, as Scala refuses a class whose self type does not conform
to the self types of the classes it inherits,
a declaration that does not conform to it,
so that inside \VAR{T} every value of \KWD{self} is an \VAR{X}.}

A trait declaration of \VAR{T} that has no \KWD{comprises} clause
may have a \emph{self parameter}:
a static parameter \VAR{X} of \VAR{T}
whose bounds include \VAR{T} at its own static parameters,
as in \EXP{\KWD{trait}\;T\llbracket{}X \KWD{extends} T\llbracket{}X\rrbracket\rrbracket},
or include an instantiation of a trait with a self parameter
that \VAR{T} also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause,
with \VAR{X} as the static argument for that self parameter.
In the bodies of the methods of \VAR{T},
\KWD{self} then has the type \EXP{T \cap X} (\secref{idn-ref}).
A trait or object declaration, or an object expression,
that extends an instantiation of \VAR{T}
must be a subtype of the static argument of that instantiation
for the self parameter of \VAR{T};
for a trait declaration with a self parameter \VAR{Y} of its own,
the requirement is on the intersection of its type and \VAR{Y}.
It is a static error otherwise.
An object declaration has no self parameter.
For example, given the declarations:
%trait Shape[\S extends Shape[\S\]\] end
%object Point extends Shape[\Point\] end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\KWD{trait}\:\TYP{Shape}\llbracket{}S \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\llbracket{}S\rrbracket\rrbracket \KWD{end}\)\\
\(\KWD{object}\:\TYP{Point} \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\llbracket\TYP{Point}\rrbracket \KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}
the following object declaration is not allowed:
%(* Not allowed! *)
%object Mark extends Shape[\Point\] end
\begin{Fortress}
\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Not allowed! \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
\(\KWD{object}\:\TYP{Mark} \KWD{extends} \TYP{Shape}\llbracket\TYP{Point}\rrbracket \KWD{end}\)
\end{Fortress}

\subsection{The type of \KWD{self} in a trait with a self parameter}
\seclabel{revival-self-param}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{idn-ref}; \secref{trait-decls}; \secref{methods}.
\item[Change] In \secref{idn-ref}, a sentence after the one on the self-type
idiom: in a trait declaration with no \KWD{comprises} clause and a self
parameter \VAR{X}, \KWD{self} has the type \EXP{T \cap X} in the bodies of the
trait's methods, and the \KWD{self} parameter keeps the type \VAR{T} in the
signature of each method declaration.
In \secref{trait-decls}, a paragraph after the one on \KWD{comprises} clauses
defines a self parameter: a static parameter of a trait with no
\KWD{comprises} clause that is bounded by the trait at its own static
parameters, or by an instantiation of a trait with a self parameter that the
trait also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause, with that static parameter as the
static argument for the self parameter.
The paragraph requires every trait or object declaration and every object
expression that extends an instantiation of such a trait to be a subtype of
the static argument of that instantiation for the self parameter, a trait with
a self parameter of its own standing as the intersection of its type and that
parameter, and gives an example marked ``Not allowed''.
In \secref{methods}, a box after the sentence that a functional method's
\KWD{self} parameter implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object
says that the sentence still holds of the declaration's signature.
Each of the three passages has a box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 13~October 2026 on the bodies of the self-typed traits,
and its second form of a self parameter, through a trait that the trait
extends, follows a default taken under that decision on 14~October 2026.
\library\ declare their orders and their algebra as traits whose static
parameter is bounded by the trait itself, as in
\EXP{\KWD{trait}\;\TYP{Integral}\llbracket{}I \KWD{extends} \TYP{Integral}\llbracket{}I\rrbracket\rrbracket},
and give them default bodies that return \KWD{self} where that parameter is
declared, or pass it where the parameter is expected: the team's minimal
complete definitions, such as \OPR{MIN} on \TYP{StandardTotalOrder} and
\VAR{floor} on \TYP{Integral}.
The interpreter runs them; the compiled type checker refused 29 of them,
since it typed \KWD{self} as the trait.
A bound constrains the static argument, not \KWD{self}: an object may extend
\EXP{\TYP{Integral}\llbracket\mathbb{Z}32\rrbracket} without being a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and a body that treats \KWD{self} as the parameter is sound
only if every declaration that extends the trait is a subtype of its static
argument for that parameter.
Scala states that rule for its declared self types (``the self type of a class
or object must conform to the self types of all classes which are inherited by
the template''); the revival reads the self type from the bound, which \library\
already write, as the team's compiled type checker reads it from a
\KWD{comprises} clause (\secref{idn-ref}), a reading that the team's gated test
\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXX10k.test} pins.
Naden's account of the Return Type Rule (2012) asked that the self-type idiom
become ``a separate construct which cannot be used as a first class type, but
instead only in bounds''
(\nolinkurl{Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex}, lines 626--630).
The signatures keep the type of the trait because the type group's account of
overloading of 2019 (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, POPL 2019) assumes, for the
completeness of its matching of types, that no declared type holds a type
parameter inside an intersection (pp.~11:21--22), and its Return Type Rule
compares declared domains (p.~11:13): with the intersection in the signatures,
the domains of the two declarations of \OPR{CMP} on \TYP{StandardPartialOrder}
and \TYP{StandardTotalOrder} became equivalent, and the compiled type checker
reported 18 errors of the Return Type Rule that the declarations do not make.
The second form of a self parameter keeps valid as written the mixins of
\library\ that the team wrote in 2009, \TYP{ContainmentBySubset} and
\TYP{ContainmentByComparison}, whose static parameter is bounded by the trait
\TYP{Containment}, which they extend at it.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md} and
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-self-type/decision-record.md} in the
revival's repository.
\item[Effect] The compiled type checker types \KWD{self} as \EXP{T \cap X} in
the bodies of the dotted and functional methods of a trait with a self
parameter \VAR{X}, keeps \VAR{T} in the signatures that overloading, the Return
Type Rule and the choice of a declaration at a call read, and refuses a trait
or object declaration or an object expression that the new paragraph of
\secref{trait-decls} does not allow, reporting that the declaration extends the
instantiation, whose self parameter is the static argument, but is not a
subtype of it.

\item[Change] In \secref{idn-ref}, a sentence after the one on the self-type
idiom: in a trait declaration with no \KWD{comprises} clause and a self
parameter \VAR{X}, \KWD{self} has the type \EXP{T \cap X} in the bodies of the
trait's methods, and the \KWD{self} parameter keeps the type \VAR{T} in the
signature of each method declaration.
In \secref{trait-decls}, a paragraph after the one on \KWD{comprises} clauses
defines a self parameter: a static parameter of a trait with no
\KWD{comprises} clause that is bounded by the trait at its own static
parameters, or by an instantiation of a trait with a self parameter that the
trait also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause, with that static parameter as the
static argument for the self parameter.
The paragraph requires every trait or object declaration and every object
expression that extends an instantiation of such a trait to be a subtype of
the static argument of that instantiation for the self parameter, a trait with
a self parameter of its own standing as the intersection of its type and that
parameter, and gives an example marked ``Not allowed''.
In \secref{methods}, a box after the sentence that a functional method's
\KWD{self} parameter implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object
says that the sentence still holds of the declaration's signature.
Each of the three passages has a box.

revival's decision of 13~October 2026 on the bodies of the self-typed traits,
and its second form of a self parameter, through a trait that the trait
extends, follows a default taken under that decision on 14~October 2026.
\library\ declare their orders and their algebra as traits whose static
parameter is bounded by the trait itself, as in

# Decision record: the comprises clause in the 2012 reading (rung X, climb batch 7C)

This is the decision record the S1 form asks for (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md`, 2026-09-26, S1): the revised passage, the original, the new text, why it changed, and the way back. Appendix I's entry "The traits that extend a closed trait" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1246-1338`, section I.1.20 of the built specification) names this file. The base is `715816bdd`. "The Working Draft of February 2011" is the unrevised copy under `Specification-1.0-frozen/` (POSITIONS 2026-09-26, the first of the batch-5 answers); the base's `Specification/basic/traits.tex:234-247` equals the frozen copy's `:229-242` line for line (`diff`, no output), so the frozen note is `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/traits.tex:230-241`, its first sentence `:231-235`.

The decision this rung carries out is the `comprises` decision (POSITIONS 2026-09-28, `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause, "Option 1."): the compiled checker learns the 2012 reading of `comprises`, the later Types chapter's (`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick:384-390`) and Welterweight's, by the narrow accommodation `everyKnownSubtypeListed`, "with an S1 callout in `Specification/basic/traits.tex` in place of the draft note at `:234-246`". Its content for the specification is the judgement's section 3, "The specification change, in the S1 form" (`explorations/reviews/anyintegral-comprises-judgement.md:100-109`). Rung Y builds the checker beside this rung and is not in this rung's tree; section 6 lists every statement the revised text makes that the gather checks against Y's landed code and tests.

## 1. The list

The list, written before any edit and committed first (`36012a2bb`), is `probes/list.txt`, from `probes/list/grep-comprises.txt` (104 hits of `comprise`, `immediate sub`, `immediately extend` and `ComprisingType` in the base's tracked `.tex` files outside `Specification/library/apis/`, each read with ten lines either side). One passage revised (R1, the note); eight left because the decision or R1 settles them (L1 to L8); four left and reported because neither the decision nor Y's section settles their new text (P1 to P4, section 4); six groups of hits outside the criterion (N1 to N6). The brief's starting list (the batch record, section 3, X) is contained in it: `traits.tex:156-170` (L1, L2), `:234-246` (R1), `:264-290` (L3); `types-vals-vars.tex:568-610` (P1); `var-ref.tex:63-70` (L4); `source-code.tex:372-392` (L5); `overloading.tex:282-305` (P2); `future.tex:269-280` (N5). The list adds P3 (`Specification/basic/functions.tex:370-415`), P4 (`Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:428-434`), the grammars (L6) and the library chapters' clauses (L7).

## 2. What the revision states, and what it does not

The revised passage (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:235-252`) states, for a trait `T` whose declaration has a `comprises` clause:
- every listed type extends `T`, and every value of type `T` is a value of one of the listed types;
- a listed type may be an instantiation of a parameterized trait, provided every static variable occurring in its static arguments is a static parameter of `T` ("static parameter" before the gather; decision 4);
- a trait or object that explicitly extends `T` is a subtype of a listed type, or a trait with a `comprises` clause of its own each of whose listed types meets the same requirement, or a trait with static parameters that at least one trait or object extends and every trait or object extending it is a subtype of a listed type;
- for a parameterized `T`, the same of each instantiation, the listed types instantiated alike.

It does not state: whether a bare static parameter (a type variable) may be listed, which is not this rung's (the batch record, section 3, X, "The decisions"; row 407 rests its home on `traits.tex:163-170`, which the edit leaves); any rule about declarations in other units, which the checker's limit makes a ledger row (Y's) and the Appendix I entry names as an effect, not a rule; anything about the ellipsis, whose sentence is kept word for word in its note (`:268-274`); anything about the `Molecule` example (`:292-325`), unchanged. So it states no more than the decision and Y's section build (the batch record's stop).

## 3. The passage: the original, the new text, the reason, route C

- Original, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:235-246` at the base (frozen `:230-241`), a `\note`, which a release build renders as nothing (`Specification/fortress/fortress.tex:35-36`): "If a trait declaration of T includes a comprises clause then the traits listed in its comprises clause are exactly the traits that immediately extend T and they must explicitly extend T (i.e., list T in their extends clause). If the comprises clause of a trait T includes "..." (and must therefore be in an API), then in a component exporting the enclosing API, other traits may explicitly extend T, but these traits may not be declared or imported by the API (see § apis)." Appendix I quotes it whole.
- New text, `traits.tex:235-252`, rendered normative text: "If a trait declaration of T includes a comprises clause then every type listed in its comprises clause extends T, and every value of type T is a value of one of the listed types. A listed type may be an instantiation of a parameterized trait, provided that every static variable that occurs in its static arguments is a static parameter of T. A trait or object that explicitly extends T must be a subtype of a listed type, unless it is a trait with a comprises clause of its own each of whose listed types meets this requirement, or a trait with static parameters such that at least one trait or object extends it and every trait or object that extends it is a subtype of a listed type. If T has static parameters, these statements hold of each instantiation of T, with the static parameters of T in the listed types replaced by the corresponding static arguments." The callout follows at `:253-267`; the note, now its second sentence alone, at `:268-274`.
- Reason: the decision. The later Types chapter reads a clause as coverage, "An instantiation of the generic type defined by such a declaration is covered by the union of the types in this set and the corresponding instantiations of the generic type in this set" (`types.tick:387-390`), the set holding "types and generic types determined by the generic type of the declaration" (`:384-386`), where G determines G' "if every parameter of G' is a parameter of G" (`:277-279`). Welterweight: "the comprises clause, if present, indicates that no value can belong to the trait unless it also belongs to one of the comprised types" (`Papers/Welterweight/grammar.tick:21-22`), and its rule D-Trait asks each listed type to be a subtype of the trait at its own parameters (`Papers/Welterweight/fig-wellformeddecls.tick:53`) and nothing of the traits that extend it (`:38-62`). The type group's later word weighs more (POSITIONS 2026-09-23) and the Types chapter is cited beside `Specification/` where it covers a topic (POSITIONS 2026-09-26, the lineage note). The note restated Sukyoung Ryu's checker rule of 2009 and is in the draft by 2009-11-06 (`explorations/reviews/anyintegral-comprises-ways.md` section 1).
- The callout, `revival-comprises`: what the Working Draft said, the reading adopted with its two sources, why a parameterized trait with a static parameter `T` lacks can be listed only at particular arguments and when it may stand unlisted, and that it answers the third question of Victor Luchangco's note at `:166-170`, whether an instantiation may be listed (worded so at the gather, on the skeptic's correction 4).

So the third case holds, and the clause is valid under the new text as written. The team's comment on the line, "not yet: `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]`" (`.fsi:434`), records the closure the five spell out.
- Route C: the same under route C; there the self-typed traits carry `comprises` clauses of their own, and a parameterized trait between a closed trait and its listed types meets the requirement through its own clause (the second case), so the third case is not needed (the judgement, section 3, "Route C"). The entry says "not needed" rather than the judgement's "never reached": in the shadow's order the new disjunct is tested before the own-clause case (`explorations/reviews/anyintegral-comprises-ways/shadow-thc.py:45-49`), so the code reaches it; the text's third case is simply not required.

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv

# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

RAW="$OUT/raw"

RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

}

For method declarations, we must take into account the self parameter,
as follows:

A \emph{dotted method declaration $\Ps_0.\f(\Ps):\Us$} is a dotted
method declaration with name $f$, where $\Ps_0$ is the trait or object
type in which the declaration appears, $\Ps$ is the parameter type,
and $\Us$ is the return type.  (Note that despite the suggestive
notation, a dotted method declaration does not explicitly list its
self parameter.)

A \emph{functional method declaration $\f(\Ps):\Us$ with self
parameter at $i$} is a functional method declaration with name $f$,

of the parameter type $\Ps$, and return type $\Us$.  Note that the static
type of the self parameter is the trait or object trait type in which

\subsection{The type of \KWD{self} in a trait with a self-type parameter}
\seclabel{revival-self-type}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{idn-ref}; \secref{trait-decls}; \secref{methods}.
\item[Change] In \secref{idn-ref}, a sentence after the one on the self-type
idiom: in a declaration of a trait \VAR{T} with no \KWD{comprises} clause and a
self-type parameter \VAR{X}, \KWD{self} has the type \EXP{T \cap X} in the bodies of
the trait's methods, and the \KWD{self} parameter keeps the type \VAR{T} in the
signature of each method declaration.
In \secref{trait-decls}, a paragraph after the one on \KWD{comprises} clauses
defines a self-type parameter: a static parameter of a trait with no
\KWD{comprises} clause that is bounded by the trait at its own static
parameters, or by an instantiation of a trait with a self-type parameter that the
trait also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause, with that static parameter as the
static argument for the self-type parameter.
The paragraph requires every trait or object declaration and every object
expression that extends an instantiation of such a trait to be a subtype of
the static argument of that instantiation for the self-type parameter, a trait with
a self-type parameter of its own standing as the intersection of its type and that
parameter, and gives an example marked ``Not allowed''.
In \secref{methods}, a box after the sentence that a functional method's
\KWD{self} parameter implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object
says that the sentence still holds of the declaration's signature.
Each of the three passages has a box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 13~October 2026 on the bodies of the self-typed traits,
and its second form of a self-type parameter, through a trait that the trait
extends, follows a default taken under that decision on 14~October 2026.
\library\ declare their orders and their algebra as traits whose static
parameter is bounded by the trait itself, as in

# Decision record: the type of `self` in a trait with a self-type parameter (rung S, climb batch 14)

This is the decision record the S1 form asks for (POSITIONS, "The S1 form"; the `fortress-repo` skill's `references/specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", part 4): each changed passage, the original and the new text, the reason, and the way back. Appendix I's entry "The type of `self` in a trait with a self-type parameter" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3296-3412`, `\seclabel{revival-self-type}`) names this file. The base is `5bf8a7c84`. "The Working Draft of February 2011" is the unrevised copy under `Specification-1.0-frozen/`.

The decision this rung carries out is P-146, "The checker reads `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type (way 6)", from the judgement's recommendation (`explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md`, section 4), with the default the coordinator took under it after the batch record's review and listed for review (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-14.md:86`): a trait's type parameter bounded by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at that parameter counts as the trait's self parameter too, never an object's. The form follows P-95 and P-96.

## 1. A word, before the passages

The specification already says "self parameter" for the parameter named `self` of a method (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:167-181`, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:577`, `:591`, `:631`, `:644`, `Specification/preliminaries/overview.tex:1140-1146`). The checker's code and the record call the trait's static parameter that `self` is read as "the self parameter" (`SelfParamDisambiguator.selfParam`; the judgement, way 6). So the text calls the static parameter a **self-type parameter**, and keeps "self parameter" for `self`. The checker's message keeps the record's wording, "whose self parameter is A" (the batch record, section S, "Rule (b), not yet built"), which reads as the instantiation's argument for the trait's static self parameter.

## 2. The passages

### 2.1 The type of `self` (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex`, section "Identifier References")

- Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:53-54` and `:64-69`, the same text as the base's `var-ref.tex:53-54`, `:64-69`, unchanged by this rung: "The type of `self` is the type of the trait or object being declared by the innermost enclosing trait or object declaration or object expression." and the self-type idiom, "If the innermost enclosing such construct is a trait declaration (for a trait called, say, `T`), and that trait declaration has a `comprises` clause, and `U_1`, `U_2`, ..., `U_n` are the traits mentioned in the `comprises` clause, then the type of `self` is instead `T ∩ (U_1 ∪ U_2 ∪ ... ∪ U_n)`."
- New text, `var-ref.tex:70-79`, after the idiom's sentence: "If that trait declaration has no `comprises` clause and has a self-type parameter `X` (§ trait-decls), a static parameter bounded by the trait itself at its own static parameters, as in `trait T[\X extends T[\X\]\]`, or by a trait with a self-type parameter that `T` extends at `X`, then the type of `self` in the bodies of its methods is instead `T ∩ X`; the `self` parameter keeps the type `T` in the signature of each method declaration, which overloading and the choice of a declaration at a call read." #!/bin/bash
# The gate's checker-count stage: run the bytecode compiler's static checker over the
# INTERPRETER's library, with the interpreter's prelude in scope, and print the per-api
# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table was produced, 1 if it could not be. 20 s in the main tree,
# measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of
# perf-probes/prelude/run-all.sh:33-35. A copy of a tracked source goes stale silently,
# so the checksum of the tracked one is recorded here and the table's "#shadow" line
# says whether it still matches.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false, read
# at OverloadingChecker.scala:77), since 2026-09-27 (climb batch 7). The memo is keyed on
# declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api's
# overloading check runs (perf-probes/nat/triage.md section 1; FACTS.md, "The hidden
# layer, classified"); with it off every build gives one count. The table's "#cache"
# row says so. On the tree of 2026-09-27 the count is 62 with the memo on and off,
# because the FortressLibrary api stops before its overloading check.
set -u
STOCK_SHA=16e6e11df9341a67038b7d7cc9f0d7bb5e5a6149019f09e92545a8b646363a0b   # ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java, 2026-09-22
OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count"
TARGET=Library/FortressLibrary.fss
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/checker-count.$$}
STOCK=$FH/ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java
OVERLOAD_CACHE=false     # the overloading checker's memo, off: see the header
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)

content.content:
== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

# Rung S, climb batch 14: the checker's self type, read from a trait's F-bound, with its extender check

- problem: the distance's classes S1 and R4, 29 of its 85 sites, the self-typed bodies of the library that return or pass `self` where the trait's parameter is declared: explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-13b/gate/distance.txt:16-17
- spec: the type of `self`, "the type of the trait or object being declared", with the self-type idiom under a `comprises` clause: Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:53-54
- precedent: the checker's own self type under a `comprises` clause (rule (a)), at the base ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:68-69; the judgement's measured patch (explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md:241-360); for rule (b)'s object expressions, checkObjectExprComprises at the base ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:70-100
- deviation: the self parameter is also read through a bound naming a self-typed trait that the trait extends at it (the coordinator's default), so the pass now takes the name environment: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:139-198, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Disambiguator.java:145
- deviation: the patch's own-name test also accepts the trait's api-qualified name, for a trait read back from an analysed api: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:124
- deviation: the specification names the trait's static parameter a self-type parameter, since "self parameter" already names a method's `self`: Specification/basic/traits.tex:285-286
- historical: ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/SelfParamDisambiguator.scala, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/FunctionalMethod.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Disambiguator.java, ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeHierarchyChecker.scala, Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex, Specification/basic/traits.tex, Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3296

Base `5bf8a7c84`, branch `wip/rung-self-type`, worktree `/home/user/fortress-selftype`, seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base14` (exit 0). Commits: `0c257d40f` (the tests), `7612a9477` (the checker), `65148acda` (the specification and the decision record), and this report's.

## 1. What changed and why

P-146 decides way 6: in a trait `C[\X\]` with no `comprises` clause whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`, `self` in the method bodies is `C[\X\] & X`; the signatures keep `C[\X\]`; whatever extends such a trait at another type is refused. The coordinator's default, on the review list, adds a second way to be the self parameter: a parameter bounded by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at that parameter (`ContainmentBySubset[\T extends Containment[\T\]\] extends Containment[\T\]`), never an object's.

- Rule (a), `SelfParamDisambiguator.scala`. The judgement's patch, applied with `git apply` on the base with no offset (114 lines, two files), then widened. `selfParam` (`:106-110`) returns the self parameter as a `VarType` and the trait's self type lists it (`:74-79`), so `TypeAnalyzer.removeSelf` gives `C[\X\] & X` as under `comprises X`. `selfIndex` (`:112-135`): first the patch's test, a type parameter bounded by the trait at its own parameters (`:116-129`); then, with an environment, `throughBound` (`:139-156`): the bound is a trait type that the trait's own `extends` clause lists too (compared by `NodeComparator`, `:175-176`), its trait is resolved as `TypeDisambiguator` resolves a name (`resolveTrait`, `:179-198`: `apiName` and `hasQualifiedTypeCons` for a qualified name, else `explicitTypeConsNames`, then `onDemandTypeConsNames`, one result, `typeConsIndex`), and that trait's self position holds `X`. The bound's own self position is read from its self type when it was disambiguated already (an analysed api), else from its header by the same two rules, with a set of names visited (`selfIndexOf`, `:160-173`). The companion's `selfParamPosition` (`:238-254`) reads a declaration's self position back from its self type, for rule (b). `Disambiguator.java:145`, `:300` pass the `TopLevelEnv` built just before; with no environment the pass reads the F-bound alone (`:44-45`).
- The confinement, `FunctionalMethod.java`, the judgement's patch unchanged: when the trait's self type was read from the F-bound (no clause, a non-empty self list), the index entry's self type and its self parameter's type are the plain trait type (`:46-60`, `:66-67`, `:88`, `:153-166`); the body's `self` is bound from the declaration's own parameters (`typechecker/impls/Decls.scala:198`) and keeps the intersection.
- Rule (b), `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala`. `checkDeclSelfParams` (`:110-132`), called beside `checkDeclComprises` (`:62`), which it does not touch: for each extended `C[\A\]` whose `C` has a self position `k` (`selfParamArg`, `:171-182`), the declaration's self type (its own type, or `D[\..\] & Y` when it has a self parameter `Y`) must be a subtype of `A_k`, else "D extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A_k, but D is not a subtype of A_k." `checkObjectExprSelfParams` (`:137-168`, called at `:65`), in the shape of `checkObjectExprComprises`: every object expression, its static parameters in scope, its type the intersection of what it extends, "An object expression extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A_k, but the object expression is not a subtype of A_k."
- The specification, in the S1 form: rule (a)'s sentence in the self paragraph (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:70-79`, callout `:80-90`); the self-type parameter and rule (b) in "Trait Declarations" with a Not-allowed example (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:285-316`, callout `:317-326`); a callout at the sentence that a functional method's `self` "implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object" (`traits.tex:599-603`), which stays true of the signature; the Appendix I entry `revival-self-type` before "Passages not yet revised" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3296-3412`); the decision record (`decision-record.md`). Built: both `ant` targets `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, "Output written on fortress.pdf (673 pages, 2305229 bytes)", no undefined reference (`grep -c "LaTeX Warning: Reference\|multiply defined\|^! Undefined control sequence"` prints 0); the outputs removed with `git clean -fXq -- Specification`.

No library line, no walk file, no code-generator file changed.

## 1. What changed and why

P-146 decides way 6: in a trait `C[\X\]` with no `comprises` clause whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`, `self` in the method bodies is `C[\X\] & X`; the signatures keep `C[\X\]`; whatever extends such a trait at another type is refused. The coordinator's default, on the review list, adds a second way to be the self parameter: a parameter bounded by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at that parameter (`ContainmentBySubset[\T extends Containment[\T\]\] extends Containment[\T\]`), never an object's.

- Rule (a), `SelfParamDisambiguator.scala`. The judgement's patch, applied with `git apply` on the base with no offset (114 lines, two files), then widened. `selfParam` (`:106-110`) returns the self parameter as a `VarType`, and the trait's self type lists it (`:74-79`), so `TypeAnalyzer.removeSelf` gives `C[\X\] & X` as under `comprises X`. `selfIndex` (`:112-135`): first the patch's test, a type parameter bounded by the trait at its own parameters (`:116-130`); then, with an environment, `throughBound` (`:139-156`): the bound is a trait type that the trait's own `extends` clause lists too (compared by `NodeComparator`, `:175-176`), its trait is resolved as `TypeDisambiguator` resolves a type name (`resolveTrait`, `:178-195`: `apiName` and `hasQualifiedTypeCons` for a qualified name, else `explicitTypeConsNames`, then `onDemandTypeConsNames`, one result, `typeConsIndex`), and that trait's self position holds `X`. The bound's own self position is read from its self type when it was disambiguated already (an analysed api), else from its header by the same two tests, with a set of names visited (`selfIndexOf`, `:158-173`). The companion's `selfParamPosition` (`:237-254`) reads a declaration's self position back from its self type, for rule (b). `Disambiguator.java:145`, `:300` pass the `TopLevelEnv` built just before; with no environment the pass reads the F-bound alone (`:44-45`).

# Rung S (climb batch 14): record lines

## For FACTS

**The compiled checker reads a self-typed trait's `self` as the implementing type, from its F-bound, keeps the signatures plain, and refuses an extender at another type.** In a trait with no `comprises` clause, a type parameter `X` bounded by the trait at its own parameters, or by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at `X`, is the trait's self parameter: `self` in its dotted and functional method bodies is `C[\X\] & X` (`SelfParamDisambiguator.selfParam`), while each functional method's signature keeps `C[\X\]` (`FunctionalMethod.parameters`), so overloading, the Return Type Rule and call resolution see no intersection. A trait or object declaration, or an object expression, that extends `C[\A\]` must be a subtype of `A` at the self position, "D extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A, but D is not a subtype of A." (`TypeHierarchyChecker.checkDeclSelfParams`, `checkObjectExprSelfParams`); an object has no self parameter. What it means: the library's 29 self-typed bodies check, and the distance is 55 on the rung's own tree (85 before, `FortressLibrary.fss:130` gone too); walk is unchanged and loads what the rule refuses; a compiled body returning `self` fails verification (row 695); the rule refuses `ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss:97-98` (NEW-S-1) and `Library/PureList.fsi:41` (row 355) and accepts the `Containment` mixins and `Relation`. Tests: `compiler_tests/SelfTypeFromBound`, `SelfTypeMixinBound`, `SelfTypeExtenderThroughOwn`, `XXXSelfTypeExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeObjectExprWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinObject`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md`, sections 1, 4 and 7.

## Ledger notes

- Row 695, append: Reproducer since climb batch 14 rung S: `compiler_tests/SelfTypeReturnSelfRunLink.test` (link, green) and `XXXSelfTypeReturnSelfRun.test` (run, expected failure: `REACHED`, then `VerifyError: Bad return type` in `XXXSelfTypeReturnSelfRun$\=Shape?XXXSelfTypeReturnSelfRun\%Pt?$DefaultTraitMethods.twin?0`). The checker accepts such a body since P-146 (rung S), so any compiled program that runs one meets the row.
- Row 407, append: Under P-146 (climb batch 14 rung S) the compiled checker reads a self type from an F-bound with no clause, so the self-typed traits need no `comprises T`; walk is untouched and this row stays open.
- Row 488, append: On climb batch 14 rung S's tree the distance's `FortressLibrary.fss:130` site (`BIG LEXICO`'s body) is absent again (55 sites), read as this row's variation.
- Row 355, append: Since climb batch 14 rung S the checker also refuses `:41` by the self-type rule: "PureList.fsi:41:27-38: PureList.List[\E\] extends Equality[\E\], whose self parameter is E, but PureList.List[\E\] is not a subtype of E." (the distance driver over `Library/PureList.fss`, `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md` section 6).

## New rows

Section "3. Traits, objects and components":

| NEW-S-1 | the team demo `ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss:97-98` declares `object generator(...) extends StandardTotalOrder[\trip\]`, which the self-type rule refuses: a `generator` is not a `trip`, though `StandardTotalOrder`'s default bodies read `self` as its parameter; walk loads and runs the demo | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug (tests) | `basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations" | `ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss` | climb batch 14 rung S | The compiled checker, by the distance stage's driver over the demo (`DistanceMulti -order check -setting any ... ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss`, `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md` section 6), reports "trips.fss:98:13-38: generator extends StandardTotalOrder[\trip\], whose self parameter is trip, but generator is not a subtype of trip."; walk has no static types and loads it. The object defines `CMP` at `generator` (`:100`), so by reading its declared order is `StandardTotalOrder[\generator\]`. No gated test reads the demo under the checker. |

## Handover

Rung S landed the checker's self type (P-146, way 6, with the coordinator's mixin default on the review list): the 29 sites gone and `:130`, the distance 85 to 55 on its own tree, the count 1, no stall (FortressLibrary 847 s); the trips demo and `PureList` refused by the extender rule (NEW-S-1, row 355), the `Containment` mixins accepted; row 695's reproducer is in place for a code-generator rung.

## Revival change

### The change

- The team's sources: the specification typed `self` as the type of the enclosing trait, and as its intersection with the listed types only under a `comprises` clause (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:53-54`, `:63-69`); the team's compiled checker built the self type the same way (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:68-71` before this change), so it refused the library's default bodies that return or pass `self` where the trait's own parameter is declared, as `floor(self):I = self` in `trait Integral[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:691`), "Function body has type Integral[\I\], but declared return type is I."; walk ran them, having no static types. Nothing checked that a type extending such a trait is an instance of its argument: `object Bad extends Shape[\Pt\]` compiled.
- What the tree now does: in a trait with no `comprises` clause whose type parameter `X` is bounded by the trait itself at its own parameters, or by a self-typed trait that it extends at `X`, the compiled checker types `self` in the method bodies as `C[\X\] & X`, keeps `C[\X\]` in the signatures, and refuses a trait or object declaration or an object expression that extends `C[\A\]` without being an `A` ("D extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A, but D is not a subtype of A."); an object never has such a parameter. Tests: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/SelfTypeFromBound`, `SelfTypeMixinBound`, `SelfTypeExtenderThroughOwn`, `XXXSelfTypeExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeObjectExprWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinObject`. The specification says so (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:70-90`, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:285-326`, `:599-603`, Appendix I `revival-self-type`). Walk is unchanged; a compiled body returning `self` still fails verification at class load.
- The reason, as evidence: the checker's refusal of 29 of the library's bodies, the team's minimal complete definitions of its orders, algebra and arrays (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:226-293`, `:360`, `:363`, `:691-724`, `:2182-2194`), all accepted after with no new refusal in the library; Scala's rule that a class's self type must conform to the self types of the classes it inherits (*Scala Language Specification 2.13*, section 5.1); Naden's "a separate construct which cannot be used as a first class type, but instead only in bounds" (`Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:626-630`). The signatures stay plain because the 2019 account of overloading (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu) assumes declared types with no type parameter inside an intersection (pp. 11:21-22) and compares declared domains in its Return Type Rule (p. 11:13): with the intersection in the signatures the checker reported 18 errors of the Return Type Rule between the `CMP` declarations of `StandardPartialOrder` and `StandardTotalOrder` that the declarations do not make. The second form of the parameter keeps the team's 2009 mixins `ContainmentBySubset` and `ContainmentByComparison` (`Library/Containment.fsi:22-30`) valid as written.

### Provenance

Batch 14's question QS, answered by P-146 ("The checker reads `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type (way 6)."), from `explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md`, section 4; the second form of the self parameter is the coordinator's default under P-146, on the review list (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-14.md:86`); built by climb batch 14's rung S.

- precedent: the checker's own self type under a `comprises` clause, which rule (a) reads from the bound instead, at the base ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:68-69; the judgement's measured patch (explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md:241-360); for rule (b)'s object expressions, checkObjectExprComprises, at the base ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:70-100

## 1. What changed and why

P-146 decides way 6: in a trait `C[\X\]` with no `comprises` clause whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`, `self` in the method bodies is `C[\X\] & X`; the signatures keep `C[\X\]`; whatever extends such a trait at another type is refused. The coordinator's default, on the review list, adds a second way to be the self parameter: a parameter bounded by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at that parameter (`ContainmentBySubset[\T extends Containment[\T\]\] extends Containment[\T\]`), never an object's.

- Rule (a), `SelfParamDisambiguator.scala`. The judgement's patch, applied with `git apply` on the base with no offset (114 lines, two files), then widened. `selfParam` (`:106-110`) returns the self parameter as a `VarType`, and the trait's self type lists it (`:74-79`), so `TypeAnalyzer.removeSelf` gives `C[\X\] & X` as under `comprises X`. `selfIndex` (`:112-135`): first the patch's test, a type parameter bounded by the trait at its own parameters (`:116-130`); then, with an environment, `throughBound` (`:139-156`): the bound is a trait type that the trait's own `extends` clause lists too (compared by `NodeComparator`, `:175-176`), its trait is resolved as `TypeDisambiguator` resolves a type name (`resolveTrait`, `:178-195`: `apiName` and `hasQualifiedTypeCons` for a qualified name, else `explicitTypeConsNames`, then `onDemandTypeConsNames`, one result, `typeConsIndex`), and that trait's self position holds `X`. The bound's own self position is read from its self type when it was disambiguated already (an analysed api), else from its header by the same two tests, with a set of names visited (`selfIndexOf`, `:158-173`). The companion's `selfParamPosition` (`:237-254`) reads a declaration's self position back from its self type, for rule (b). `Disambiguator.java:145`, `:300` pass the `TopLevelEnv` built just before; with no environment the pass reads the F-bound alone (`:44-45`).
- The confinement, `FunctionalMethod.java`, the judgement's patch unchanged: when the trait's self type was read from the F-bound (no clause, a non-empty self list), the index entry's self type and its self parameter's type are the plain trait type (`:43-61`, `:66-67`, `:88`, `:152-166`); the body's `self` is bound from the declaration's own parameters (`typechecker/impls/Decls.scala:198`) and keeps the intersection.
- Rule (b), `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala`. `checkDeclSelfParams` (`:105-133`), called beside `checkDeclComprises` (`:62`), which it does not touch: for each extended `C[\A\]` whose `C` has a self position `k` (`selfParamArg`, `:170-181`), the declaration's self type (its own type, or `D[\..\] & Y` when it has a self parameter `Y`) must be a subtype of `A_k`, else "D extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A_k, but D is not a subtype of A_k." `checkObjectExprSelfParams` (`:135-168`, called at `:65`), in the shape of `checkObjectExprComprises`: every object expression, its static parameters in scope, its type the intersection of what it extends, "An object expression extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A_k, but the object expression is not a subtype of A_k."
- The specification, in the S1 form: rule (a)'s sentence in the self paragraph (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:70-79`, callout `:80-90`); the self-type parameter and rule (b) in "Trait Declarations" with a Not-allowed example (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:285-316`, callout `:317-326`); a callout at the sentence that a functional method's `self` "implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object" (`traits.tex:599-603`), which stays true of the signature; the Appendix I entry `revival-self-type` before "Passages not yet revised" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3296-3412`); the decision record (`decision-record.md`). Undefined control sequence" Specification/fortress/fortress.log` prints 0; the outputs removed with `git clean -fXq -- Specification`.

# Rung S (climb batch 14): record lines

## For FACTS

**The compiled checker reads a self-typed trait's `self` as the implementing type, from its F-bound, keeps the signatures plain, and refuses an extender at another type.** In a trait with no `comprises` clause, a type parameter `X` bounded by the trait at its own parameters, or by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at `X`, is the trait's self parameter: `self` in its dotted and functional method bodies is `C[\X\] & X` (`SelfParamDisambiguator.selfParam`), while each functional method's signature keeps `C[\X\]` (`FunctionalMethod.parameters`), so overloading, the Return Type Rule and call resolution see no intersection. A trait or object declaration, or an object expression, that extends `C[\A\]` must be a subtype of `A` at the self position, "D extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A, but D is not a subtype of A." (`TypeHierarchyChecker.checkDeclSelfParams`, `checkObjectExprSelfParams`); an object has no self parameter. What it means: the library's 29 self-typed bodies check, and the distance is 55 on the rung's own tree (85 before, `FortressLibrary.fss:130` gone too); walk is unchanged and loads what the rule refuses; a compiled body returning `self` fails verification (row 695); the rule refuses `ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss:97-98` (NEW-S-1) and `Library/PureList.fsi:41` (row 355) and accepts the `Containment` mixins and `Relation`. Tests: `compiler_tests/SelfTypeFromBound`, `SelfTypeMixinBound`, `SelfTypeExtenderThroughOwn`, `XXXSelfTypeExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeObjectExprWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinObject`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md`, sections 1, 4 and 7.

## Ledger notes

- Row 695, append: Reproducer since climb batch 14 rung S: `compiler_tests/SelfTypeReturnSelfRunLink.test` (link, green) and `XXXSelfTypeReturnSelfRun.test` (run, expected failure: `REACHED`, then `VerifyError: Bad return type` in `XXXSelfTypeReturnSelfRun$\=Shape?XXXSelfTypeReturnSelfRun\%Pt?$DefaultTraitMethods.twin?0`). The checker accepts such a body since P-146 (rung S), so any compiled program that runs one meets the row.
- Row 407, append: Under P-146 (climb batch 14 rung S) the compiled checker reads a self type from an F-bound with no clause, so the self-typed traits need no `comprises T`; walk is untouched and this row stays open.
- Row 488, append: On climb batch 14 rung S's tree the distance's `FortressLibrary.fss:130` site (`BIG LEXICO`'s body) is absent again (55 sites), read as this row's variation.
- Row 355, append: Since climb batch 14 rung S the checker also refuses `:41` by the self-type rule: "PureList.fsi:41:27-38: PureList.List[\E\] extends Equality[\E\], whose self parameter is E, but PureList.List[\E\] is not a subtype of E." (the distance driver over `Library/PureList.fss`, `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md` section 6).

## New rows

Section "3. Traits, objects and components":

| NEW-S-1 | the team demo `ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss:97-98` declares `object generator(...) extends StandardTotalOrder[\trip\]`, which the self-type rule refuses: a `generator` is not a `trip`, though `StandardTotalOrder`'s default bodies read `self` as its parameter; walk loads and runs the demo | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug (tests) | `basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations" | `ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss` | climb batch 14 rung S | The compiled checker, by the distance stage's driver over the demo (`DistanceMulti -order check -setting any ... ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss`, `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md` section 6), reports "trips.fss:98:13-38: generator extends StandardTotalOrder[\trip\], whose self parameter is trip, but generator is not a subtype of trip."; walk has no static types and loads it. The object defines `CMP` at `generator` (`:100`), so by reading its declared order is `StandardTotalOrder[\generator\]`. No gated test reads the demo under the checker. |

## Handover

Rung S landed the checker's self type (P-146, way 6, with the coordinator's mixin default on the review list): the 29 sites gone and `:130`, the distance 85 to 55 on its own tree, the count 1, no stall (FortressLibrary 847 s); the trips demo and `PureList` refused by the extender rule (NEW-S-1, row 355), the `Containment` mixins accepted; row 695's reproducer is in place for a code-generator rung.

## Revival change

### The change

- The team's sources: the specification typed `self` as the type of the enclosing trait, and as its intersection with the listed types only under a `comprises` clause (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:53-54`, `:63-69`); the team's compiled checker built the self type the same way (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/disambiguator/SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:68-71` before this change), so it refused the library's default bodies that return or pass `self` where the trait's own parameter is declared, as `floor(self):I = self` in `trait Integral[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:691`), "Function body has type Integral[\I\], but declared return type is I."; walk ran them, having no static types. Nothing checked that a type extending such a trait is an instance of its argument: `object Bad extends Shape[\Pt\]` compiled.
- What the tree now does: in a trait with no `comprises` clause whose type parameter `X` is bounded by the trait itself at its own parameters, or by a self-typed trait that it extends at `X`, the compiled checker types `self` in the method bodies as `C[\X\] & X`, keeps `C[\X\]` in the signatures, and refuses a trait or object declaration or an object expression that extends `C[\A\]` without being an `A` ("D extends C[\A\], whose self parameter is A, but D is not a subtype of A."); an object never has such a parameter. Tests: `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/SelfTypeFromBound`, `SelfTypeMixinBound`, `SelfTypeExtenderThroughOwn`, `XXXSelfTypeExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeObjectExprWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinExtenderWrong`, `XXXSelfTypeMixinObject`. The specification says so (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:70-90`, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:285-326`, `:599-603`, Appendix I `revival-self-type`). Walk is unchanged; a compiled body returning `self` still fails verification at class load.
- The reason, as evidence: the checker's refusal of 29 of the library's bodies, the team's minimal complete definitions of its orders, algebra and arrays (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:226-293`, `:360`, `:363`, `:691-724`, `:2182-2194`), all accepted after with no new refusal in the library; Scala's rule that a class's self type must conform to the self types of the classes it inherits (*Scala Language Specification 2.13*, section 5.1); Naden's "a separate construct which cannot be used as a first class type, but instead only in bounds" (`Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:626-630`). The signatures stay plain because the 2019 account of overloading (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu) assumes declared types with no type parameter inside an intersection (pp. 11:21-22) and compares declared domains in its Return Type Rule (p. 11:13): with the intersection in the signatures the checker reported 18 errors of the Return Type Rule between the `CMP` declarations of `StandardPartialOrder` and `StandardTotalOrder` that the declarations do not make. The second form of the parameter keeps the team's 2009 mixins `ContainmentBySubset` and `ContainmentByComparison` (`Library/Containment.fsi:22-30`) valid as written.

### Provenance

Batch 14's question QS, answered by P-146 ("The checker reads `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type (way 6)."), from `explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md`, section 4; the second form of the self parameter is the coordinator's default under P-146, on the review list (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-14.md:86`); built by climb batch 14's rung S.
